name: delivery
character: What leaves the building: the master profile with the gating mode it is really measured in, sample rate and bit depth, the mux target, and the tolerances the video gate judges.

streaming.reference: web / social delivery: full-program integrated loudness

youtube.reference: YouTube normalises to about -14 LUFS on playback and turns down only

prime.reference: Amazon Prime Video delivery spec: -24 LKFS +/-2, full program

broadcast.reference: EBU R128: -23 LUFS +/-0.5, -1 dBTP; ATSC A/85 uses -24 LKFS +/-2 in the US

netflix.reference: Netflix Sound Mix Specifications: -27 LKFS +/-2 LU dialogue-gated (ITU-R BS.1770-1), -2 dBTP

cinema.reference: cinema print master: dialogue-gated anchor, -2 dBTP

sources: https://www.rtw.com/blog/rtw-knowledge-base-1/worldwide-loudness-delivery-standards-4 (EBU R128 -23 LUFS, ATSC A/85 -24 LKFS, YouTube -14 LUFS)
https://tech.ebu.ch/docs/r/r128s4.pdf (dialogue loudness is measured on the speech part; do not raise dialogue to programme loudness)
https://voicedeck.io/tools/platform-delivery-spec-card/ (Prime Video and Disney+ are full-program gated at -24 LKFS)

provenance.master_profiles.broadcast.lufs: EBU R128 -23 LUFS (+/-0.5); the tolerance is widened to 1.0 here
provenance.gate.dialogue_band_min_db: starting value: 12 dB of music below the voice in 1-4 kHz; positive because the figure is 'how far the music sits under', the same sign as dialogue_snr_min_db
